knowledge_point.title: Applying the Vector Form of the Chain Rule to a Function of Three Variables

question.:question/worked-solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x + y - 2 z)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x + y - 2 z)\,j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(x + y - 2 z)\,k \\  & =(1)\,i+(1)\,j+(-2)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=t,y=t^{2},$ and $z=t$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =(1)\,i+(1)\,j+(-2)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t^{2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,k \\  & =(1)\,i+(2 t)\,j+(1)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =((1)\,i+(1)\,j+(-2)\,k)\cdot ((1)\,i+(2 t)\,j+(1)\,k) \\  & =(1)\cdot (1)+(1)\cdot (2 t)+(-2)\cdot (1) \\  & =(1)+(2 t)+(-2) \\  & =2 t - 1.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: If $f(x,y,z)=- x - 3 y + 2 z$ and $r(t)=(t)\,i+(t^{2})\,j+(t^{2})\,k,$ compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))].$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(- x - 3 y + 2 z)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(- x - 3 y + 2 z)\,j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(- x - 3 y + 2 z)\,k \\  & =(-1)\,i+(-3)\,j+(2)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x=t,y=t^{2},$ and $z=t^{2}$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =(-1)\,i+(-3)\,j+(2)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t^{2})\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t^{2})\,k \\  & =(1)\,i+(2 t)\,j+(2 t)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =((-1)\,i+(-3)\,j+(2)\,k)\cdot ((1)\,i+(2 t)\,j+(2 t)\,k) \\  & =(-1)\cdot (1)+(-3)\cdot (2 t)+(2)\cdot (2 t) \\  & =(-1)+(- 6 t)+(4 t) \\  & =- (2 t + 1).\end{aligned}
$$
